annotations.title: Match my resume to a job

description: Matches the user's resume against one job posting: the job match score (0-100), each requirement of the posting judged met, partial, missing or unverifiable with the resume's own words as evidence, and the posting's keywords the resume lacks. The score comes from a published, deterministic rubric (the same file gets the same score from the same engine on the same day), not from an AI model; present it as the rubric's result, not your own judgement. Use it only on the user's own resume, at their request: it is a tool for candidates. Never use it to screen, rank, compare or reject other people. Runs locally and reads only the files named in the call; nothing is sent anywhere.

job_path.description: Path to a job posting: .txt, .md, .pdf, .docx, or a saved .html page. Give job_path or job_text.

job_text.description: The job posting as text. Give job_path or job_text, not both.

language.description: Read the resume and the posting in this language (en, de, fr, hi, es, pt; en: English only). Default: detected from each. Give it only when the resume was read in the wrong language; a posting in another language needs that language.

path.description: Absolute path to the user's resume: .pdf, .docx, .html, .txt, .md, or a .json JSON Resume or ats-resume document. Give path or text, not both.

region.description: Read the resume as from this country (US, DE, FR, GB, IN, ES, BR, PT, MX, AR, CO, CL). Default: inferred from it.

text.description: The resume as plain text, when there is no file. Give path or text, not both.

name: match_job

jobMatchScore.description: 0-100, how well the resume meets the posting.

missingKeywordGroups.description: The same terms by kind; soft skills weigh less in the match.

requirements.description: Each requirement of the posting, judged.
